title: Tabular evolution adapter observation
description: What one engine did with one transition of one scenario, under one operation and mode. One record per line of a JSON Lines results file. Records observations only: no field says whether the outcome is correct, expected or acceptable, and results never modify the corpus.

schema_version.description: Version of this record format, independent of the manifest schema_version.

corpus_version.description: The corpus release the fixtures belong to, e.g. 0.1.0.

corpus_revision.description: The exact commit the fixtures were read from: the git commit of the checkout, or the Hugging Face commit when read from the Hub.

inputs.description: The versions read, in the order they were passed to the engine; each is `from` or `to`.

adapter_version.description: Version of the engine the adapter drives, as the engine reports it.

operation.description: read_each_version: read one version on its own (one record per input). read_versions_together: read `from` and `to` as one dataset.

mode.description: The engine-specific variant of the operation, e.g. union_by_name, positional, unified_permissive, diagonal_relaxed; `default` when the engine's default behaviour is used.

result_schema.description: Top-level fields of the result, in result order; null when status is error.

error_class.description: Qualified class name of the exception the engine raised; null when status is success.

notes.description: Free-text detail, e.g. the engine's error message verbatim, or a native type with no corpus equivalent. Never an operation variant (that is `mode`).

type.description: The type in the corpus type vocabulary (src/tabular_evolution/types.py), or null when the engine's type has no clear equivalent there. When `nullable` is null, nested members carry no `not null`: the engine records no nullability, and the missing marker is not an observation.

native_type.description: The type as the engine spells it, verbatim.

nullable.description: The engine's nullability flag for the field; null when the engine records none.
